messages:
Frank (CEO): Thanks for the great all-hands. Quick live Q&A: can we get a crisp "why we win / why we lose" summary for leadership and GTM playbooks? Looking for concrete asks and suggested product mitigations.

Hannah (PM): I'll kick this off. From product reviews + win/loss interviews we compiled: wins: strong SLA + Dedicated offering, clear pricing buckets for cost predictability, and our migration tooling for cache/state. losses: customers price compare vs owning infra, missing on-prem/offline option for regulated industries, and occasional inference quality drift after model swaps.

Maya (CRO): Sales color: wins often close when we can commit to throughput and provide references that show cost per 1M tokens. Losses are usually when procurement can't justify the premium vs self-host or when the customer needs private-air-gapped deployment.

Ellie (CS): Support sees churn signals around two patterns: 1) repeated latency variance during peak windows, 2) lack of rollback/"pin to previous model" UX after deployments. Both cause escalations and renewal friction.

Liam (Eng): Possible product mitigations: expose "pin version" toggle in Console + API; add rollout canaries with automatic fallback based on quality/latency metrics; increased observability (per-request model id in traces). I can draft an RFC.

Ravi (Data): On the feedback loops side: we should instrument "reason_lost" and "primary_ask" tags on closed deals and map them to support ticket categories. Example schema: [deal_id, lost_reason, requested_feature, churned_within_90d]. I can produce the first 30 rows.

Hannah (PM): Good. Leadership want a prioritized list: what's the one product feature or policy that, if shipped in 90 days, would move the needle most? My pick: "on-prem deployable package + audit logs" for finance/health customers. Second: first-party fine-tuning/workflow in the Console. Thoughts?

Maya (CRO): I agree. For the top 3 customer asks from last quarter: 1) On-prem/VPC appliance, 2) predictable committed pricing for Dedicated, 3) model pinning & automated rollback. We should turn each into a one-pager for sales.

Frank (CEO): From leadership: we can prioritize on-prem + auditability for Q1 if Sales can show 2-3 near-term prospects that require it. Otherwise, invest in pinning/rollback which helps retention broadly.

Liam (Eng): Note on scope: an on-prem appliance with KMS integration + audit logs is nontrivial (security review, installers, support model). We can build a slim "air-gapped runtime" first and add orchestration later.

Ellie (CS): I'll collect three anonymized renewal calls that reference "rollback" and "auditing" so Product can see verbatim asks.

Ravi (Data): Running the CRM tag counts now. Quick preview: 'need_onprem' = 6, 'sla_commit' = 12, 'pin_model' = 9 for deals since 2025-09-01. I'll paste the dataset link when done.

Hannah (PM): Action items: 1) Maya -> collate two live deals that hinge on on-prem (due Tue). 2) Liam -> draft RFC for pin/rollback + telemetry (due Fri). 3) Ellie -> upload the customer snippets and renewal notes (due Wed). 4) Ravi -> full tag counts and small table mapping asks to churn risk (due Tue). Owners acknowledged?

Maya (CRO): Acknowledged. I'll also anonymize and share the RFP snippets.

Liam (Eng): Acknowledged. Will include estimated effort and a minimal viable ship.

Ellie (CS): Acknowledged 1 I'll add context and recommended rebuttals for sales.

ops-bot: created doc `playbooks/win-loss-summaries/q4-2025` by @Hannah

Frank (CEO): Love this. One final ask: when we present to the board, can we show a simple metric: "avoidable churn" by feature (e.g., percent of churn attributable to lack of on-prem or rollback)? If Ravi can model that, leadership will have a clear signal.

Ravi (Data): I'll model a conservative estimate and include confidence bands. Expect a first draft by Tue afternoon.

Hannah (PM): Perfect. I'll synthesize this into the all-hands follow-up email with links to the playbook folder. Thanks team!
